questions.stem: What are the components of a triglyceride?

options.text: Three amino acids and one glycerol
Three glucose molecules and one fatty acid
Three fatty acids and one glycerol
One fatty acid and one glycerol

questions.explanation: A triglyceride is made of one glycerol molecule bonded to three fatty acid chains through ester bonds formed by condensation reactions.

questions.stem: What type of bond links fatty acids to glycerol in a lipid?
questions.explanation: Ester bonds (also called ester linkages) are formed between the fatty acids and glycerol by condensation reactions, with the release of three water molecules per triglyceride.

questions.stem: What is the difference between saturated and unsaturated fatty acids?

options.text: Saturated fatty acids have no double bonds between carbon atoms; unsaturated have one or more

questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds and are straight chains. Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds, creating kinks in the chain.

questions.stem: Why are lipids good for long-term energy storage?

options.text: They can be broken down without enzymes
They contain more energy per gram than carbohydrates

questions.explanation: Lipids contain approximately twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates, making them very efficient for long-term energy storage in the body.

questions.stem: What is the function of phospholipids?

options.text: They form the bilayer structure of cell membranes

questions.explanation: Phospholipids have a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and two hydrophobic (water-repelling) tails, allowing them to form the bilayer structure of cell membranes.

questions.stem: Which type of fat is linked to an increased risk of heart disease?
questions.explanation: Saturated fats are linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease because they can raise blood cholesterol levels, leading to fatty deposits in arteries.

questions.stem: Apart from energy storage, name one other function of lipids in the body.

options.text: Thermal insulation and protection of organs

questions.explanation: Lipids provide thermal insulation (subcutaneous fat keeps the body warm), protect vital organs from physical damage, and form waterproof layers on skin and leaves.
